newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi Stock Exchange plans to start evening trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi Stock Exchange plans to start evening trade.

text.p: India's Delhi Stock Exchange (DSE) plans to start a 90-minute evening trading session, a senior official of the exchange said on Tuesday.

"The government's policy decisions many times come late in the day, as do company results. Why not open trading and let markets reflect these announcements immediately," S.S. Sodhi, chief executive officer, DSE, told Reuters.
DSE plans to implement the second session of trading in the next several months, Sodhi said. The evening trading will start at 6.00 p.m. (1230 GMT) and end at 7.30 p.m. (1400 GMT).
The Delhi bourse, India's third largest, currently trades from 9.45 a.m. (0415 GMT) to 3.45 p.m. (1015 GMT).
Sodhi said that the evening session would increase trading volumes by between 20 percent to 25 percent.
"Many deals happen on the kerb, as there is no exchange open in the evenings. The more kerb deals we bring into the exchange, the better it is for the exchange," he said.

At present, the trading volume of the DSE is in the region of 2.5 billion rupees to 3.0 billion rupees a day. Sodhi says that tradng volumes have steadily climbed since the introductio of online trading in March 1996.

"What holds us back from reaching the seven billion rupee volumes of the Bombay Stock Exchange is that we don't have institutional buying in Delhi," he said. "So we have to develop other USPs to attract investors to DSE."
Apart from plans for the evening session, which would be the first time for an Indian stock exchange, Sodhi said that DSE was also in the process of setting up a stock clearing corporation.
A clearing corporation is a body that guarantees a trade, and makes payments to brokers selling if need be. This leads to an increase in the trading volume due to higher liquidity.
"The DSE Clearing Corporation Ltd will have a corpus of over one billion rupees, and should be operational by the end of the year," Sodhi said.
